paper_title: Developing Story Case Studies of Generative AI's Use in Journalism
caption: : The distribution of different input stimulus material types provided by journalists to LLMs, over the WildChat conversations that are matched to online articles from the two identified news agencies.
model_annotation: The donut chart illustrates the distribution of different stimulus types used by journalists as input material for large language models (LLMs) during WildChat conversations that were matched to online articles from two identified news agencies. The chart is divided into nine segments, each representing a distinct stimulus type with its corresponding percentage. The largest segment, colored dark red, is "Draft/Other" at 26.4%, followed by "Press Release" (18.7%, gold) and "External News Article" (18.1%, dark green). Other categories include "Interview" (8.8%, dark blue), "Organizational Report" (7.7%, purple), "Event Posting" (6.6%, brown), "Organizational Website" (4.9%, light purple), "Intra-agency news article" (4.9%, light blue), and "Email" (2.7%, light green). The smallest segment, "Social Media Post" (1.1%, orange), is visually the thinnest slice. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order around the central white circle labeled "Stimulus Type," with each category clearly labeled with its name and percentage value directly adjacent to its respective slice. The chart does not include a separate legend, as the labels are directly tied to their corresponding segments.
